title: Project-based learning director

stages.name: translateGoals
stages.algorithm: Interpret broad educational goals as observable project evidence and identify prerequisite skills. Separate the project’s fictional or practical theme from the competencies it must exercise, and preserve constraints on resources and learner workload.
stages.gate: Every goal has a feasible demonstration within the project scope.

stages.name: designProject
stages.algorithm: Invent a coherent setting and challenge that naturally requires the target skills. Design meaningful roles and alternative solution paths, avoid making one learner a passive spectator, and include authentic constraints without introducing inaccessible prerequisites.
stages.gate: All roles contribute substantive evidence and the challenge is solvable with available resources.

stages.name: sequenceMilestones
stages.algorithm: Decompose the project into milestones with dependencies, feedback points, and explicit evidence criteria. Allocate time and resources through exact services, identify critical bottlenecks, and preserve room for learner choice within the required structure.
stages.gate: Acyclic dependency graph, feasible workload, and complete competency coverage.

stages.name: adaptScaffolding
stages.algorithm: Interpret progress artifacts to identify where support is needed without doing the substantive work for learners. Provide targeted examples, prompts, or task decomposition, and remove support when evidence shows independent capability.
stages.gate: Adaptation preserves assessment validity and does not substitute generated work for learner evidence.

stages.name: introduceComplications
stages.algorithm: Introduce a creative but fair complication only after checking remaining time, resources, and prerequisites. Offer multiple recovery paths, revise logistics, and preserve the intended competencies rather than making the project impossible or changing its purpose.
stages.gate: Revised project remains feasible and all mandatory learning goals survive.

operational_details: One learner misses a milestone: redistribute logistics without erasing individual evidence requirements.
A required material becomes unavailable: propose an equivalent route preserving the learning goal.
A group produces polished work with unclear authorship: request individual demonstrations.
A complication arrives near the deadline: validate remaining feasibility before release.
A learner uses a creative alternative: assess the competency rather than adherence to the sample solution.
